minutes.headline: Select Board found On the Rocks bar in violation twice, imposed a 7-day 8 p.m. closing, then renewed its license 2-1.
minutes.summary: The board held a liquor license violation hearing for On the Rocks (overcrowding and a fight), found two violations 3-0 and set a seven-day early-closing penalty. It ratified the recreation director and assistant town accountant appointments, handled license renewals, and debated the charge for a municipal building design committee including a cost cap. The meeting ended in executive session on litigation.

public_comment.topic: A parks commissioner, speaking for herself, urged that the recreation director appointment be put on hold until the role's reporting and coordination with the Parks Commission are set up.
A resident of Rose Garden Lane raised noise and safety concerns about On the Rocks and its patio, asking whether these can be considered at license renewal.

what_happened.line: The Select Board found the On the Rocks bar violated two liquor license regulations, on occupancy and a fight in and outside the premises, by a 3-0 vote.
The board set a seven-day penalty, December 31 through January 6, with closing at 8 p.m. and a written remedial plan required from the licensee.
The board then renewed On the Rocks' all-alcohol, Common Victualler and jukebox licenses, each by a 2-1 vote.
The board ratified the recreation director and assistant town accountant appointments.
A building design committee charge, including a project cost cap, was debated without resolution and is to be revised.

why_it_matters: The licensing decisions show how the board weighs a finding of violations against renewal: the bar faces a short early closing but keeps its licenses.

The cost cap for the municipal building design committee bears on how much the town may borrow for the project, and on whether it stays within the town's debt and fiscal policies alongside other projects.
watch_next: The revised design committee charge, with a cost cap, which the board is to amend as the town manager's financial roadmap develops.
The seven-day early-closing penalty at On the Rocks, starting December 31, and the written remedial plan due from the licensee.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every vote's outcome and on the licensing, appointment and penalty decisions. They differ mainly in captioned numbers and names (warrant amounts, section 1.03 vs 1.04, Ixtapa, officer names). The one substantive difference is the TC Passios charge: ours records a cost-cap decision with 28 and 39 million figures, while the official minutes record only a 22 million placeholder for discussion and a redraft.
